findings.finding: Gaoxy has no separately exposed physical-connection limit. HTTP and core service validators reject unknown options. Service.start_backend sets num_acceptors=1, num_connections=spec.limits.max_active, retry_count=0.

ThousandIsland supports a start-time per-acceptor live-handler cap. DynamicSupervisor max_children enforces it. At capacity it closes the accepted raw socket before starting a handler, returns too_many_connections, and emits acceptor spawn_error. No public runtime setter was found.

Lowering Gate max_active to 1 changes accounting admission and cannot retain the required connection, writer and worker leases. Fixture currently overrides max_bytes only; max_active defaults to64. Exact global active==3 is an assertion, not a configured max_active==3.

One acceptor serializes accepts but does not cap concurrent handlers to one. Public pause/suspend is not an atomic first-connection limit: Gaoxy pause changes Gate mode; TI suspend retains existing connections and observing a first connection races additional accepts.

No installed documented Chrome option reviewed establishes one socket per listener. Installed manpage explicitly says undocumented flags change; documented flags have no connection-count limiter. No guessed Chromium flags, feature names, binary-string semantics, external docs, network or browser execution used. This is a bounded negative result, not proof that all Chromium versions lack such an option.

Diagnostic2 global accounting failure is exactly explained by two real C/R pairs plus worker. Keep every actor visible and the exact global3/byte assertions unchanged. This evidence does not establish why the prior run target writer exited before authorization.
